annotationRationale: The decisive step is expressing every term as a product of two integers greater than one. The reviewed factorization method applies exactly; a geometric-series formula is unnecessary.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Number Theory is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The nth displayed-pattern term factors as R(10^n+1), where R has n+1 ones. Both factors exceed 1 for n≥1, so none of the first ten terms is prime. Choice A and the key agree; there is no figure issue.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: 2022_AMC_10B_Q06 / overlapping-strings-of-ones was independently verified against this identical question and retained once, despite appearing in both source collections. LIVE and Random Math use the same factorization. No distinct additional route is needed.
review.annotationCheck: Prime/composite classification and applications of factorization are correctly assessed. Pattern representation is sensible support. Omitting geometric-series summation is appropriate because no such formula is used.
review.areaCheck: Number Theory is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The two length-(n+1) strings occupy digit positions 0 through n and n through 2n, overlapping only at position n. Their addition creates the required middle 2 without carrying. Thus the factorization holds for every n≥1, including 121=11², and both factors are at least 11. The prime count is therefore 0.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The candidate faithfully reuses the supplied project explanation and names 2022_AMC_10B_Q06 / overlapping-strings-of-ones. Its methodLocalSources provenance is consistent, and both inherited IDs, live-reference-2022_AMC_10B_Q06 and randommath-reference-2022_AMC_10B_Q06, are retained. The current LIVE and Random Math references support the same mathematics; neither is presented as verified official MAA authorship.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The numerical example motivates the factorization, and the digit-shift explanation proves it for all ten terms. The explicit factor bounds complete the compositeness argument.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Prime/composite numbers and applications of factorization precisely describe the decisive reasoning. A geometric-series node is unnecessary, and the pattern-support node covers the general nth-term interpretation.
